name: P1 with the episodic memory keyed on the cortex against the founder key
question: On P1's development founders, with Brain.compose(..., memory_choice=True): is frozen whole-chain success after teaching at or above the founder key's when the episodic records are keyed on the cortex state of each decision (memory_key="cortex")?
scope: component prerequisite behavior in a fully observed world; a memoryless stage-aware policy solves it, so it tests no memory

sensory.note: V5's layout with the episodic memory at the library's defaults: the founder key, the observation

correct_step_qualified.note: the same caregiver with qualified teaching; a separately named numerical arm, refusals counted at the fixed budget

schedule.unit: executed decisions of the whole life

caregiver.label: the required action of the observation shown now, after an executed nonterminal mistake in a guided window

withdrawal: the acquired life resumes from its seam with the caregiver gone and learning on; a separate frozen copy is read at the end

evaluation.note: frozen copies with their own action stream; Brain.reset at every episode start equals the life's episode boundary for an act-only reader; one greedy episode, since every greedy episode from a reset reads the same deterministic answers

seeds.note: P1's five development founders, every arm under both recipes

analysis.unit: founder; a pair is one arm on one founder, sensory recipe against cortex recipe
analysis.gate: for each of the six arms: cortex minus sensory in immediate frozen sampled success (P1's primary reading), founder-paired; the cortex key meets P1 when the upper end of every interval is at or above zero
analysis.report: greedy success after teaching, sampled and greedy success after the life alone, each arm against random and the frozen founder within each recipe
